subject: Pctl tiered commitment and grace logic discussion for hosted API
messages:
From: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightwavehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API commitments — p50/p95 measurement and carveouts

Kimberly,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood’s hosted API last week. We’re drafting our SRE acceptance criteria for the PoC and need clarity on three items before we move to procurement:

1) Clear p50 / p95 numeric targets (per-region) and whether they’re per-route or global.
2) The measurement window — do you use rolling 1h, 24h, or daily aggregation for p95?
3) Grace logic for short-lived bursts and regional maintenance — how are those excluded from SLO calculations?

Our PCI-sensitive workload will be routed to us-west and we expect occasional batch inference spikes during ETL windows. We want to capture realistic failure modes so the SLA doesn’t trigger credits for known maintenance or for traffic patterns we can agree to exclude.

Can you propose a short, deterministic measurement policy and an example with a sample month so our SREs can validate detection?

Thanks,
Marco Diaz
Head of Infrastructure, Brightwave Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@brightwavehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — p50/p95 measurement and carveouts

Marco —

Appreciate the clear ask. I’ve looped in Karthik (product) to weigh in on measurement mechanics and Lauren from legal for the carveout language later in the thread. High-level proposal:

- Commitment tiers: Standard (p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 450ms), Premium (p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 280ms). Per-region bindings (us-west, us-east, eu-west) — both measured independently.
- Measurement windows: rolling 1h for alerting, 24h rolling for contractual reporting, and calendar-day aggregation for monthly SLA evaluation (30-day window).
- Burst/grace rules: we propose an automated transient carveout when we detect a short-lived traffic spike related to customer-initiated batch (defined as >5x baseline QPS sustained >2min and auto-attributed by request headers). Scheduled maintenance windows announced >=72h in advance are excluded. Emergency maintenance is eligible for a 4-hour carveout at Redwood discretion; we’ll provide post-event evidence.

I’m attaching a one-page sample calculation and a chart that shows a hypothetical month with two carveouts applied. If that aligns, we can formalize precise wording for procurement.

Next steps: Karthik, can you confirm the aggregation math and whether we should offer a regional rolling-window exception for short-lived network degradation?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sales Director, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightwavehealth.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@brightwavehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — p50/p95 measurement and carveouts

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from product/runtime:

- Measurement: p50/p95 are computed over request latency end-to-end (request-receive to final token emitted) per model-route. For hosted customers we currently calculate per-route percentiles using a 1-minute sliding histogram, then derive hourly and daily rollups from those minute buckets. For contract language we recommend using the daily aggregation (midnight UTC calendar day) to avoid timezone disputes.

- Windowing example (concrete): take all per-minute histograms for the calendar day, merge into a day histogram and compute p50/p95. For monthly SLA we compute the fraction of days in the 30-day window that meet the p95 threshold and require >= 95% of days to be within threshold for the month to be considered compliant.

- Grace logic: automated carveouts will mark per-minute buckets as excluded if the traffic spike rule (Kim’s definition) is triggered AND the customer tags the requests with the agreed batch header. Network-provider blips (third-party transit) are eligible for a transient regional carveout if packet-loss >1% across backbone ASes for >15min (we will provide traceroutes and backbone metrics).

Open question: do you want the monthly pass/fail computed by counting compliant calendar days, or by computing the monthly aggregated p95 across the full month? Counting days is kinder to customers with spikes but can be gamed; full-month aggregation is stricter. My recommendation for Brightwave (ETL-bursty) is day-counting with a 95% day pass threshold.

-Karthik
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightwavehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — p50/p95 measurement and carveouts

Marco —

Thanks for the patience. From a contracting perspective here’s proposed language to include in the SOW/SLA:

1) Definitions: "Measurement Day" means a calendar day (UTC) during which latency percentiles are computed from Redwood’s per-minute histograms. "Compliance Day" means a Measurement Day where p50 and p95 for the customer’s primary route(s) fall within the committed thresholds for the selected tier.

2) Monthly evaluation: Redwood will evaluate SLO compliance by counting Compliance Days in the preceding 30-day rolling window; the month is compliant if >= 95% of Measurement Days are Compliance Days.

3) Carveouts: (a) Pre-scheduled maintenance communicated >=72 hours in advance; (b) Customer-tagged batch windows where request header X-Redwood-Batch=true and traffic meets the agreed spike definition (>5x baseline for >2 minutes); (c) Backbone transit incidents where carrier-provided metrics show packet-loss >1% across primary transit providers for >15 minutes. Each carveout will be enumerated in Redwood’s evidence package with timestamps, affected regions, and supporting logs.

4) Credits: If a month fails the SLO evaluation, Redwood will provide service credits computed as a percentage of monthly hosted fees (table ranges by tier). Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy.

If that approach works for Brightwave we’ll prepare an SLA addendum for signature and include an example calculation appendix. Marco/Alyssa — can you confirm you’re comfortable with the day-count approach and the customer-tagging requirement for batch carveouts?

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

On a process note: Kimberly, please route procurement to include the "evidence package" link (HubSpot deal) when sending for signature so procurement has the logs to validate any future disputes.
